## Simulation: programs near the detection threshold {#sec-results-threshold}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s14
#| tbl-cap: "Programs near the detection threshold (the near-threshold simulation, rank 7). All fits converged. Planted share is the planted program's share of expression variance. Entries show supervised / two-step for recovery, false-active count and C. Difference is the mean paired validation C of the supervised fit at w_S = 1 minus the two-step fit, with the number of datasets in which the supervised fit was higher. Oracle C is the validation concordance of the true predictor."
a <- s14a[s14a$arm %in% c("twostep", "A1_w1"), ]
w1 <- a[a$arm == "A1_w1", ]; ts <- a[a$arm == "twostep", ]
k <- match(paste(w1$strength, w1$share), paste(ts$strength, ts$share))
dd <- s14d[match(paste(w1$strength, w1$share), paste(s14d$strength, s14d$share)), ]
tt <- data.frame(Survival = w1$strength, `Planted share` = pct(w1$share, 2),
  Recovered = paste(round(s14_n * w1$recovered), round(s14_n * ts$recovered[k]), sep = " / "),
  `False-active` = paste(num(w1$false_active, 1), num(ts$false_active[k], 1), sep = " / "),
  C = paste(num(w1$c_validation), num(ts$c_validation[k]), sep = " / "),
  `Difference (wins)` = paste0(sgn(dd$d.mean), " (", dd$d.wins, ")"),
  `Oracle C` = num(w1$oracle_c), check.names = FALSE)
tt <- tt[order(tt$Survival, w1$share), ]
kable(tt, row.names = FALSE)
```

In the cells of the fixed-weight and cross-validated-weight simulations the two-step fit already finds the planted program, so those simulations
cannot show what supervision adds. The near-threshold simulation, fitted at rank 7, planted weaker programs (@tbl-s14). With strong survival
the supervised fit had the higher validation concordance in
`r sum(s14p$d[s14p$strength == "strong"] > 0)` of `r sum(s14p$strength == "strong")` datasets,
and the gain grew as the program weakened. At the smallest planted share, `r pct(min(s14_shares), 2)`, the supervised fit
recovered the program in `r round(s14_n * w1$recovered[w1$strength == "strong" & w1$share == 5e-4])`
of `r s14_n` datasets, where the two-step fit recovered none, and validation concordance rose by
`r sgn(s14d$d.mean[s14d$strength == "strong" & s14d$share == 5e-4])`. With realistic survival the
two fits were close at the larger shares, and neither recovered the program at the smallest share. Both fits averaged at least one false-active program per dataset in every strong cell, the
two-step fit as many or more than the supervised fit. Their contribution to the risk score is
measured next.

The rank-5 fits of @tbl-lb-sim use the same strong-survival design at the smallest share and
give different counts, because a different number of programs is fitted. At $w_S = 1$ the
rank-5 projection model recovered the program in
`r k5s_cell("S14_strong", 5e-4, 1, "YFB")$recovery_successes` of 10 datasets with
`r num(k5s_cell("S14_strong", 5e-4, 1, "YFB")$false_active_mean, 1)` false-active programs per
fit, against `r round(s14_n * w1$recovered[w1$strength == "strong" & w1$share == 5e-4])` and
`r num(w1$false_active[w1$strength == "strong" & w1$share == 5e-4], 1)` at rank 7.

The post hoc analysis measures the variance of the sum of the nonmatched score contributions
relative to the variance of the full score. It includes nonmatched programs below the
survival-activity threshold. It also measures full-minus-matched concordance on the same
datasets. In the cross-validated-weight simulation the largest cell median variance ratio was
`r pct(max(fa13_cells$other_share), 1)`, and the largest absolute cell mean change in
concordance was `r num(max(abs(fa13_c$delta_c)))`. In the larger-share cells of the near-threshold simulation, the
corresponding ratios reached `r pct(max(fa14_larger$other_share[fa14_larger$arm == "A1_w1"]), 1)`
for the supervised fit ($w_S = 1$, block-weighted) and
`r pct(max(fa14_larger$other_share[fa14_larger$arm == "twostep"]), 1)` for the two-step fit. Across both fits the largest absolute mean change in C in those cells was
`r num(max(abs(fa14_larger$delta_c)))`. At the smallest planted share the median ratios ranged
from `r pct(min(fa14_small$other_share), 1)` to `r pct(max(fa14_small$other_share), 1)`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-near-threshold
#| fig-cap: "Near-threshold simulation at rank 7: recovery by fit and paired validation concordance differences for the unit-weight fit versus two-step. Dots in the difference panels represent datasets. Diamonds give cell means."
#| out-width: "100%"
chapter_figure("sup_sim_near_threshold")
```

## Real-data refit at the cross-validated weight {#sec-results-s15}

The largest cross-validated partial log-likelihood on the training folds occurred at $w_S = `r s15$w_star`$. Across weights `r min(s15_curve$w)` to `r max(s15_curve$w)`, it varied by `r num(diff(range(s15_curve$cvpl)), 2)`. The nested folds selected weights `r paste(s15_nested$chosen_w, collapse = ", ")`. Nested cross-validation gave mean C `r num(s15$nested_mean_C)` (SE `r num(s15$nested_se_C)`), compared with `r num(s15$s11_w1_C)` at fixed $w_S = 1$. These estimates use all comparable pairs and a preprocessed matrix. The working-model estimate in @sec-working-model uses within-cohort pairs and fold-specific scaling. Of 216 fits in the weight grid, 189 converged and 27 reached the 300-sweep cap, all in inner folds. Every selected outer fit and the full-data fit converged. The capped inner fits contributed to weight selection. At the largest tested weight, median survival precision share among active loadings was `r sci(s15_curve$share_active_median[which.max(s15_curve$w)], 1)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s15
#| tbl-cap: "Training cross-validation of the survival-block weight. The precision share is the median among active programs. The nested evaluation uses weights chosen within each outer training set. Model: supervised YFB fit (w_S = 1, 2,218 genes, rank 5) refitted at each weight."
kable(data.frame(Weight = s15_curve$w, `CV partial log-likelihood` = num(s15_curve$cvpl),
  `Mean C (SE)` = paste0(num(s15_curve$mean_C), " (", num(s15_curve$se_C), ")"),
  `Folds converged` = paste0(s15_curve$folds_converged, "/", s15_curve$folds_ok),
  `Survival precision share` = formatC(s15_curve$share_active_median, format = "e", digits = 2),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Gene screen, input scaling and rank in training cross-validation {#sec-results-rank}

```{r}
# Ranks the paired comparison cannot separate from K = 7, and the full-fit active count there.
tcv_flat <- tcv_k$K[tcv_k$K >= tcv_K & tcv_k$K <= 8]
tcv_flat_active <- unique(tcv_k$full_active[tcv_k$K %in% tcv_flat])
# The working-model CV (lb_yfb_training) is a separate run of the same configuration and folds.
tcv_k5f <- subset(tcv_cv, input == "D4_Z" & K == tcv_K)
stopifnot(nrow(tcv_k5f) == 5, setequal(tcv_k5f$fold, k5_y$fold))
tcv_run_gap <- max(abs(k5_y$C_within - tcv_k5f$C_within[match(k5_y$fold, tcv_k5f$fold)]))
stopifnot(length(tcv_flat_active) == 1, tcv_r(tcv_K, "conv") == 5,
          all(abs(tcv_k$diff_vs_K7[tcv_k$K %in% tcv_flat]) <= tcv_k$se_diff_vs_K7[tcv_k$K %in% tcv_flat] |
              tcv_k$K[tcv_k$K %in% tcv_flat] == 7))
```

Training cross-validation, run on the rank-7 reference, supported the gene screen and the
input scaling (@tbl-inputs). In concordance within cohort, the alternative screen was lower by
`r num(-tcv_in["D2_Z", "diff"])` (paired SE `r num(tcv_in["D2_Z", "se_diff"])`), division by the within-cohort standard deviation by
`r num(-tcv_in["D4_XSD", "diff"])` (SE `r num(tcv_in["D4_XSD", "se_diff"])`) and the rank
transform by `r num(-tcv_in["D4_RANKZ", "diff"])` (SE `r num(tcv_in["D4_RANKZ", "se_diff"])`).
No alternative was better, so the current screen and the z-scores within cohort stay. Each
alternative converged in more folds than the current input.

Across ranks, concordance was flat from $K = `r tcv_K`$ to `r max(tcv_k$K)`, between
`r num(tcv_plateau[1])` and `r num(tcv_plateau[2])`, and lower from $K = `r min(tcv_k$K)`$ to
`r tcv_K - 1`, between `r num(tcv_low[1])` and `r num(tcv_low[2])` (@tbl-rank). The best mean
was at $K = `r tcv_best$K`$ (`r num(tcv_best$mean_C_within)`, SE `r num(tcv_best$se_C_within)`),
so the threshold was `r num(tcv_thr)` and the one-standard-error rule selected $K = `r tcv_K`$.
Its concordance was `r num(-tcv_r(tcv_K, "diff"))` below that of $K = 7$ (paired SE
`r num(tcv_r(tcv_K, "se_diff"))`). Every fold fit at $K = `r tcv_K`$ converged,
against `r tcv_r(7, "conv")` of 5 at $K = 7$, and the full fit had `r tcv_flat_active` survival-active
programs at every rank from `r min(tcv_flat)` to `r max(tcv_flat)`. Every column kept nonzero
loadings at every rank, so the priors did not remove programs. The paired differences are much
more precise than the fold standard error used by the rule, and on that scale ranks
`r min(tcv_flat)` to `r max(tcv_flat)` cannot be told apart. The rule picks the smallest rank on
the plateau. It does not show that $K = `r tcv_K`$ predicts better than $K = 7$. Because these
comparisons are close, the five-fold cross-validation was repeated with four more random
partitions of the patients. Averaged over the five partitions, the rule again selected
$K = 5$ (concordance 0.643, against a best of 0.651 at $K = 12$). Four of the five partitions
selected $K = 5$ on their own and one selected $K = 10$. $K = 5$ converged in all 25 fold fits,
against 18 at $K = 7$. The alternative screen was 0.002 lower on average (SE 0.008), so the
screen also stays. The working model uses $K = `r tcv_K`$ (@sec-working-model), and its
programs match those of the rank-7 reference (@sec-model-states). The working-model
concordance in @sec-working-model comes from a separate run of the same configuration on the
same folds. Its fold values differ from those here by at most
`r num(tcv_run_gap)`,
so both runs give a mean of `r num(k5_cw$mean_YFB)`, with fold SE `r num(k5_se_y)` in that run
and `r num(tcv_r(tcv_K, "se"))` here.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-inputs
#| tbl-cap: "Training cross-validation of the gene screen and input scaling at rank 7 (five folds). Concordance counts only pairs of patients from the same cohort, so the rank-7 reference's value differs from the mean fold concordance in @tbl-cv. Differences are paired over folds. Convergence is within 300 sweeps."
kable(data.frame(Input = unname(tcv_inputs), Genes = big(tcv_genes),
  `Mean C (SE)` = paste0(num(tcv_in[, "mean"]), " (", num(tcv_in[, "se"]), ")"),
  `Difference from rank-7 reference (SE)` = c("", paste0(sgn(tcv_in[tcv_alt, "diff"]), " (",
                                                     num(tcv_in[tcv_alt, "se_diff"]), ")")),
  `Folds converged` = paste0(tcv_in[, "conv"], "/5"), check.names = FALSE),
  row.names = FALSE, align = "lcccc")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rank
#| tbl-cap: "Training cross-validation of the rank on the current screen with z-scores within cohort (five folds). Concordance counts only pairs within cohort. Differences from K = 7 are paired over folds. Convergence is within 300 sweeps. Survival-active programs are counted in the fit to all training patients. The one-standard-error rule selects the smallest K whose mean C reaches the best mean minus its SE."
kable(data.frame(K = tcv_k$K,
  `Mean C (SE)` = paste0(num(tcv_k$mean_C_within), " (", num(tcv_k$se_C_within), ")"),
  `Difference from K = 7 (SE)` = ifelse(tcv_k$K == 7, "",
    paste0(sgn(tcv_k$diff_vs_K7), " (", num(tcv_k$se_diff_vs_K7), ")")),
  `Folds converged` = paste0(tcv_k$folds_converged, "/5"),
  `Survival-active programs` = tcv_k$full_active,
  Selected = ifelse(tcv_k$K == tcv_K, "One-SE rule", ""), check.names = FALSE),
  row.names = FALSE, align = "cccccc")
```

## Rank and ELBO pruning {#sec-results-pruning}

The pruning simulation asks whether ELBO pruning recovers the planted program and the true
rank. For a flat coefficient likelihood the coefficient update returns the prior moments and an
exact zero coefficient KL. Ordinary and protected pruning both lost the planted program in most datasets and
retained too few programs in a simulation starting at rank `r unique(kl2$K)` (@tbl-kl2).
The working fit instead keeps all `r tcv_K` columns selected by training cross-validation.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-kl2
#| tbl-cap: "Pruning simulation. Converged counts fits whose relative change in the ELBO fell below the stopping tolerance. Outputs stable counts fits whose last-sweep change in the reconstruction and risk score was below 10^-4. The saved summary gives the count of planted-program recoveries and the median retained rank."
kable(data.frame(Arm = kl2$arm, Noise = kl2$noise,
  Recovered = paste0(kl2$recovered, "/", kl2$n),
  `Mean false-active` = num(kl2$false_active, 2),
  `Converged` = paste0(kl2$elbo_converged, "/", kl2$n),
  `Outputs stable` = paste0(kl2$outputs_converged, "/", kl2$n),
  `Median rank` = kl2$median_K, check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Comparison with other prognostic models {#sec-results-comparators}

```{r}
#| include: false
p6e <- rd(K5, "prompt6_comparators", "external.csv"); p6p <- rd(K5, "prompt6_comparators", "paired.csv")
p6h <- rd(K5, "prompt6_comparators", "pooled_hr.csv"); p6t <- rd(K5, "prompt6_comparators", "tuning.csv")
p7c <- rd(K5, "prompt7_desurv_style", "cutpoints.csv"); p7g <- rd(K5, "prompt7_desurv_style", "group_hr.csv")
p7r <- rd(K5, "prompt7_desurv_style", "program_rule.csv"); p7k <- rd(K5, "prompt7_desurv_style", "rank_paired.csv")
p7ke <- rd(K5, "prompt7_desurv_style", "rank_external.csv"); p7a <- rd(K5, "prompt7_desurv_style", "adjusted_hr.csv")
p7m <- rd("prompt7_desurv_style", "mixed_simulation.csv")
p7s13 <- rd("prompt7_desurv_style", "s13_rule.csv"); p7s14 <- rd("prompt7_desurv_style", "s14_rule.csv")
cmp_lab <- c(w1 = "Supervised", twostep = "Two-step", PurIST = "PurIST",
             elastic_net = "Elastic-net Cox", DeSurv = "DeSurv")
gp <- function(m) p7g[p7g$model == m & p7g$cohort == "pooled", ]
# Pooled HR of the supervised score, unadjusted or adjusted for a subtype call.
p7a_hr <- function(s, adj) {
  r <- p7a[p7a$model == "w1" & p7a$cohort == "pooled" & p7a$subtype == s & p7a$adjusted == adj, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1); r
}
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(p7a_hr("PurIST", FALSE)$hr, p7a_hr("DeCAF", FALSE)$hr)))
s14ts <- p7s14[p7s14$arm == "twostep", ]
```

The supervised and two-step scores in
this section are those of the supervised YFB fit ($w_S = 1$, 2,218 genes, rank 5) (@sec-model-states). Every comparator was trained on the
`r train_n[["TCGA_PAAD"]] + train_n[["CPTAC"]]` training patients only, and each score's direction was fixed on
the training data. DeSurv used the authors' code, preprocessing and published settings (rank 3),
which the authors selected on the same training cohorts [@Young2026]. The elastic-net Cox model
on the 2,218-gene set chose $\alpha = `r p6t$alpha[p6t$selected]`$ by cross-validation on the training
folds. The $\alpha = 0.75$ and lasso paths reached glmnet's iteration limit at small penalties. PurIST entered as a Cox model on its basal-like probability [@Rashid2020]. No clinical
model was fitted, because no stage, grade, age or margin field is recorded in both training
cohorts and all five external series.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-comparators
#| tbl-cap: "External performance of the fixed supervised fit and comparators trained on the same patients. Mean C is the equal-weight mean over the five series. The HR is per pooled external SD from a Cox model stratified by series, with a robust interval clustered on donor. The difference is supervised minus comparator C, averaged over series, with a 95% donor-bootstrap interval. Model: supervised YFB fit (w_S = 1, 2,218 genes, rank 5) and its two-step comparator. PurIST, elastic-net Cox and DeSurv are separate comparators trained on the same patients."
x <- aggregate(C ~ model, p6e[p6e$model %in% names(cmp_lab), ], mean)
x <- merge(x, p6h[, c("model", "hr", "donor_lo", "donor_hi")], by = "model")
x <- merge(x, p6p[, c("model", "diff", "lo", "hi")], by = "model", all.x = TRUE)
x <- x[match(names(cmp_lab), x$model), ]
cmp_tab <- data.frame(Model = unname(cmp_lab[x$model]), `Mean C` = num(x$C),
  `HR per SD (95% CI)` = paste0(num(x$hr, 2), " (", ci(x$donor_lo, x$donor_hi, 2), ")"),
  `Difference (95% CI)` = ifelse(is.na(x$diff), "", paste0(sgn(x$diff), " (", ci(x$lo, x$hi), ")")),
  check.names = FALSE)


kable(cmp_tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

The paired differences and their donor-bootstrap intervals are shown in @tbl-comparators. Unsupervised EBMF followed by Cox regression gave supervised-minus-EBMF differences of `r paste(sgn(p7k$diff), collapse = ", ")` at ranks 5, 15 and 40. At ranks 15 and 40 the unpenalized Cox step overfit, with external calibration slopes of `r num(min(p7ke$cal_slope[p7ke$model %in% c("EBMF_15", "EBMF_40")]), 2)` to `r num(max(p7ke$cal_slope[p7ke$model %in% c("EBMF_15", "EBMF_40")]), 2)`. Those differences describe that pipeline rather than the information in a larger factorization.

### Risk groups from training cutpoints {#sec-fixed-risk-groups}

For the rank-5 supervised and two-step scores, one cutpoint per score maximized the log-rank statistic
on the out-of-fold training scores, with at least 20% of patients per group. It was applied
unchanged in every external series. The cutpoints were `r num(p7c$cutpoint[p7c$model == "w1"])`
training SDs for the supervised score and `r num(p7c$cutpoint[p7c$model == "twostep"])` for the
two-step score. The pooled high-versus-low HRs were `r num(gp("w1")$hr, 2)`
(`r ci(gp("w1")$donor_lo, gp("w1")$donor_hi, 2)`) and `r num(gp("twostep")$hr, 2)`
(`r ci(gp("twostep")$donor_lo, gp("twostep")$donor_hi, 2)`). They are not comparable, because the
supervised cutpoint places `r gp("w1")$high` of `r gp("w1")$n` external records in the high-risk
group and the two-step cutpoint places `r gp("twostep")$high`. A smaller, more extreme group gives
a larger HR at equal ranking ability. The supervised score's pooled HR per training SD was
`r num(p7a_hr("PurIST", FALSE)$hr, 2)` (donor-clustered 95% CI
`r ci(p7a_hr("PurIST", FALSE)$donor_lo, p7a_hr("PurIST", FALSE)$donor_hi, 2)`) without
adjustment, `r num(p7a_hr("PurIST", TRUE)$hr, 2)`
(`r ci(p7a_hr("PurIST", TRUE)$donor_lo, p7a_hr("PurIST", TRUE)$donor_hi, 2)`) after adjusting
for PurIST subtype and `r num(p7a_hr("DeCAF", TRUE)$hr, 2)`
(`r ci(p7a_hr("DeCAF", TRUE)$donor_lo, p7a_hr("DeCAF", TRUE)$donor_hi, 2)`) after adjusting for
DeCAF.
@fig-fixed-risk displays the groups formed by the training cutpoints. The program section also gives within-series tertiles as a separate description of ranking. The out-of-fold scores used the feature matrix of the training fit, whose per-cohort scaling included held-out training-fold expression. The cutpoint search used the pooled out-of-fold training scores and their outcomes.

```{r}
#| label: fig-fixed-risk
#| fig-cap: "External Kaplan–Meier estimates by fixed training cutpoint. Each model uses its own cutpoint. Curves are drawn from saved monthly survival estimates. The numbers at risk are in Appendix C. Model: supervised YFB fit (w_S = 1, 2,218 genes, rank 5) and its two-step comparator."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 5.1
km_fixed <- rd(K5, "prompt7_desurv_style", "km_monthly.csv")
km_fixed$Series <- factor(unname(cohort_label[km_fixed$cohort]), levels = unname(cohort_label))
km_fixed$Model <- factor(unname(cmp_lab[km_fixed$model]), levels = c("Supervised", "Two-step"))
km_fixed$Group <- factor(km_fixed$high, levels = 0:1, labels = c("Low", "High"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(km_fixed$Series), !anyNA(km_fixed$Model), !anyNA(km_fixed$Group))
ggplot2::ggplot(km_fixed, ggplot2::aes(month, survival, colour = Group, linetype = Group)) +
  ggplot2::geom_step(linewidth = .45) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(Series ~ Model,
                      labeller = ggplot2::labeller(Series = ggplot2::label_wrap_gen(10))) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(Low = "#006878", High = "#B34226")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Months", y = "Estimated survival") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 0))
```

These fixed groups and the subtype-adjusted associations are exploratory. Differences between high-versus-low hazard ratios also reflect differences in the patients assigned to each group.

### Program stability in training folds {#sec-program-stability}

For the rank-5 fit, we call a program a main prognostic program when its standardized
coefficient is at least 0.25 of the largest, it accounts for at least 5% of the signed
risk-score variance and it is survival-active in at least four of the five training folds.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-program-rule
#| tbl-cap: "Main prognostic programs of the supervised training fit. The ratio is $|\\beta_k| \\mathrm{SD}(YF_k)$ relative to the largest program. The signed share is $\\mathrm{Cov}(\\eta_k, \\eta)/\\mathrm{Var}(\\eta)$. Active folds count training folds in which a loading matched with absolute correlation at least 0.7 was survival-active. The precision share is an upper bound on survival's median share of the loading precision. Model: supervised YFB fit (w_S = 1, 2,218 genes, rank 5)."
stopifnot(sum(p7r$main) == 1)
y <- p7r[p7r$active | p7r$ratio > .1, ]
kable(data.frame(Program = y$program, Active = ifelse(y$active, "Yes", "No"),
  Ratio = num(y$ratio, 2), `Signed share` = num(y$variance_share), `Active folds` = y$active_folds,
  `Main program` = ifelse(y$main, "Yes", "No"), `Precision share` = sprintf("%.1e", y$precision_share_upper),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

Program `r p7r$program[p7r$main]` is the one main prognostic program. Programs 4 and 5 were active in `r p7r$active_folds[p7r$program == 4]` and `r p7r$active_folds[p7r$program == 5]` folds. In the saved rank-7 fits of the cross-validated-weight simulation, the coefficient and variance-share criteria marked the planted program as main in `r sum(p7s13$planted_pass_partial)` of `r nrow(p7s13)` fits and marked `r sum(p7s13$false_active_dropped_partial)` of the `r sum(p7s13$false_active_denominator)` false-active programs as minor. In the two-step fits of the near-threshold simulation they marked `r sum(s14ts$false_active_dropped_partial)` of `r sum(s14ts$false_active_denominator)` as minor. Fold stability was not computed in simulation.

### Mixed-signal simulation {#sec-mixed-signal}

A simulation fitted at rank 7 planted one strong and one near-threshold
prognostic program with equal standardized effects at 2,000 genes.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mixed
#| tbl-cap: "Mixed-signal simulation at rank 7, ten datasets per arm. All fits converged and every arm recovered the strong program in every dataset. Precision is the fraction of the 50 genes with the largest absolute fitted loading on the matched program that lie in the planted support. The mean includes datasets whose best match has absolute correlation below 0.7."
m <- p7m[p7m$direction == "near_threshold", ]
z <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(m, m$arm), function(a) data.frame(arm = a$arm[1],
  rec = sum(a$recovered), n = nrow(a), prec = mean(a$top50_precision), C = mean(a$C))))
z <- z[match(c("twostep", "A1_w1", "A2_w1", "A1_w5"), z$arm), ]
kable(data.frame(Arm = c("Two-step", "Supervised, w_S = 1", "Supervised, joint $\\beta$, w_S = 1",
  "Supervised, w_S = 5"), `Near-threshold recovered` = paste0(z$rec, "/", z$n),
  `Top-50 precision` = num(z$prec), `Validation C` = num(z$C), check.names = FALSE),
  row.names = FALSE)
```

At $w_S = 1$ the supervised and two-step fits recovered the near-threshold program equally
often. A fixed $w_S = 5$ lost it in most datasets and had lower validation C.

### Recovery across simulation designs {#sec-recovery-synthesis}

All three designs compared here fit rank 7. The matched two-step fit recovered the planted program in the representative cell of the cross-validated-weight simulation. The largest unit-weight recovery difference in the near-threshold simulation favoured the supervised fit and occurred at the smallest planted share with strong survival (@tbl-s14). In the mixed-signal simulation, the two unit-weight fits had the same near-threshold recovery as the two-step fit. @fig-recovery-synthesis shows the accompanying differences in false activity, convergence and calibration. On PDAC data the loading agreement and the small Cox contribution to loading precision are consistent with an effect through the coefficient fit (@sec-results-loadings).

```{r}
#| label: fig-recovery-synthesis
#| fig-cap: "Matched simulation results, all fitted at rank 7. The cross-validated-weight simulation panel shows the 1% planted-variance cell with the cross-validation-selected weight in the block-weighted fit. The near-threshold simulation panel shows the smallest planted share at both survival strengths. The mixed-signal cell reports recovery of the weaker loading and uses one row per fit for false activity and convergence. Calibration slopes were not saved for the mixed-signal experiment."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 5.3
s13_cell <- subset(s13, cell == "v0.01" & arm == "A1")
s13_two <- subset(rd("yfb_supervision_strength_2026-11-05", "twostep.csv"), cell == "v0.01")
stopifnot(nrow(s13_cell) == 1L, nrow(s13_two) == s13_cell$n)
design_s13 <- data.frame(
  Design = "Cross-validated weight, 1% share",
  Fit = c("Two-step", "Supervised"),
  Recovery = c(mean(s13_two$recovered), s13_cell$recovered / s13_cell$n),
  False_active = c(mean(s13_two$false_active), s13_cell$mean_false_active),
  Convergence = c(mean(s13_two$converged), s13_cell$converged / s13_cell$n),
  Calibration = c(median(s13_two$cal_slope), s13_cell$slope_median))
s14_focus <- subset(s14, share == min(share) & arm %in% c("A1_w1", "twostep"))
mixed_focus <- subset(p7m, direction == "near_threshold" & arm %in% c("A1_w1", "twostep"))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(mixed_focus[c("seed", "arm")]))
s14_focus$Design <- paste("Near threshold,", s14_focus$strength)
mixed_focus$Design <- "Mixed signal"
mixed_focus$cal_slope <- NA_real_
replicates <- rbind(s14_focus[c("Design", "arm", "recovered", "false_active", "converged", "cal_slope")],
                    mixed_focus[c("Design", "arm", "recovered", "false_active", "converged", "cal_slope")])
design_means <- aggregate(cbind(recovered, false_active, converged) ~ Design + arm,
                          replicates, mean)
calibration <- aggregate(cal_slope ~ Design + arm, replicates, median)
design_means <- merge(design_means, calibration, by = c("Design", "arm"), all.x = TRUE)
designs <- rbind(design_s13, data.frame(
  Design = design_means$Design, Fit = ifelse(design_means$arm == "twostep", "Two-step", "Supervised"),
  Recovery = design_means$recovered, False_active = design_means$false_active,
  Convergence = design_means$converged, Calibration = design_means$cal_slope))
designs$Design <- factor(designs$Design,
  levels = c("Cross-validated weight, 1% share", "Near threshold, strong", "Near threshold, realistic", "Mixed signal"))
measures <- c(Recovery = "Proportion recovered", False_active = "Mean false-active count",
              Convergence = "Proportion converged", Calibration = "Median calibration slope")
panel <- stack(designs[names(measures)])
panel$Design <- rep(designs$Design, times = length(measures))
panel$Fit <- rep(designs$Fit, times = length(measures))
panel$Measure <- factor(unname(measures[panel$ind]), levels = unname(measures))
ggplot2::ggplot(panel, ggplot2::aes(Design, values, fill = Fit)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(position = "dodge", width = .7, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(data = data.frame(Measure = factor("Median calibration slope", levels = levels(panel$Measure))),
                     ggplot2::aes(yintercept = 1), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Measure, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(Supervised = "#006878", `Two-step` = "#D39631")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 22, hjust = 1),
                 legend.position = "bottom")
```


# Programs of the supervised fit {#sec-biology}

The programs and external associations in this section are from the rank-5 working model (@sec-model-states). Programs `r andj(program_active)` were survival-active. Program 2's protective pole includes classical epithelial and exocrine genes. Program 4's adverse pole includes acinar genes, with immune-associated genes at the opposite pole. Program 5 has an adverse coefficient and mitotic and stromal-immune enrichment. These descriptions do not identify a cell type or establish tumor-intrinsic biology.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-programs
#| tbl-cap: "Programs of the supervised training fit. Coefficients are log hazard ratios per SD of the program score, with posterior SDs in parentheses. The positive and negative poles list the genes with the largest signed loadings in each direction. Model: supervised YFB fit (w_S = 1, 2,218 genes, rank 5)."
kable(data.frame(Program = programs$program,
  `Coefficient (SD)` = paste0(num(programs$beta), " (", num(programs$beta_sd), ")"),
  Active = ifelse(programs$active, "yes", "no"),
  `Positive pole` = programs$top_pos, `Negative pole` = programs$top_neg,
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-program-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Scaled loadings of selected genes across the fitted programs. Asterisks indicate survival-active programs. Model: supervised YFB fit (w_S = 1, 2,218 genes, rank 5)."
#| out-width: "100%"
chapter_figure("sup_programs_heatmap_k5")
```

## Enrichment and published signatures {#sec-program-interpretation}

Enrichment was calculated on signed loadings among the modeled genes. The leading sets are in @tbl-enrichment.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-enrichment
#| tbl-cap: "Leading enrichment at each pole of the survival-active programs. NES denotes normalized enrichment score. The p-values are adjusted within program. Model: supervised YFB fit (w_S = 1, 2,218 genes, rank 5)."
finite_enrichment <- subset(program_enrich, is.finite(padj))
enrich_groups <- split(finite_enrichment,
                       list(finite_enrichment$program, sign(finite_enrichment$NES)), drop = TRUE)
enrich_top <- do.call(rbind, lapply(enrich_groups, function(x) x[which.min(x$padj), ]))
enrich_top <- enrich_top[order(enrich_top$program, -sign(enrich_top$NES)), ]
set_label <- sub("^(HALLMARK|REACTOME|KEGG)_", "", enrich_top$set)
set_label <- gsub("_", " ", set_label)
# DeSurv program sets are named by content, not by DeSurv's program numbers.
set_label <- sub("DeSurv D1 ClassicalTumor", "DeSurv classical tumor", set_label)
set_label <- sub("DeSurv D2 StromalImmune", "DeSurv stromal-immune", set_label)
set_label <- sub("DeSurv D3 BasalLikeTumor", "DeSurv basal-like tumor", set_label)
stopifnot(!any(grepl("\\bD[0-9]\\b", set_label)))
kable(data.frame(Program = enrich_top$program, Collection = enrich_top$collection,
  `Gene set` = set_label, NES = num(enrich_top$NES, 2),
  `Adjusted p` = formatC(enrich_top$padj, format = "e", digits = 2),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

Spearman correlations with published signatures were computed within series using the
available standardized expression genes. In the pooled training data, Program 2 was inversely associated with the Moffitt basal-like signature, and Program 4 was positively associated with the Bailey ADEX signature. The corresponding external ranges are in @tbl-signatures.
Correlations between Program 5 and the stromal-immune signature were weaker. These
descriptive associations characterize fixed programs.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-signatures
#| tbl-cap: "Spearman correlations with selected subtype and stromal signatures. The external interval is the range of point estimates across series. PurIST uses the saved basal-like probabilities. Model: supervised YFB fit (w_S = 1, 2,218 genes, rank 5)."
signature_pairs <- data.frame(program = program_active,
  signature = c("Moffitt basal-like", "Bailey ADEX", "DeSurv stromal-immune"))
signature_rows <- merge(signature_pairs, program_subtype, by = c("program", "signature"))
training_sig <- subset(signature_rows, cohort == "Pooled training")
external_sig <- subset(signature_rows, cohort %in% names(cohort_label))
external_purist <- subset(program_subtype, program %in% program_active &
  grepl("PurIST", signature) & cohort %in% names(cohort_label))
stopifnot(nrow(training_sig) == length(program_active),
          nrow(external_sig) == length(program_active) * nrow(e_w1),
          nrow(external_purist) == length(program_active) * nrow(e_w1))
sig_range <- tapply(external_sig$spearman_r, external_sig$program,
                    function(z) ci(min(z), max(z), 2))
purist_range <- tapply(external_purist$spearman_r, external_purist$program,
                       function(z) ci(min(z), max(z), 2))
kable(data.frame(Program = training_sig$program, Signature = training_sig$signature,
  Training = num(training_sig$spearman_r, 2),
  External = unname(sig_range[as.character(training_sig$program)]),
  `External PurIST` = unname(purist_range[as.character(training_sig$program)]),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

The loadings of the supervised fit and of the $w_S = 0$ fit agreed at $|r| = `r num(min(matched_loadings$abs_r))`$ for every
matched program (@sec-results-loadings).

## Evidence for the individual programs {#sec-program-profiles}

Program 2 combines the clearest external direction agreement with survival activity in
`r p7r$active_folds[p7r$program == 2]` training folds. Its protective pole is associated
with classical epithelial and exocrine expression. Its adverse pole includes hypoxia
and glycolysis genes. The separate external Cox estimates agree in direction with its
training coefficient across all scored series.

Program 4 was active in `r p7r$active_folds[p7r$program == 4]` training folds. Its positive pole includes acinar genes and its negative pole includes immune-associated genes. Its external estimates follow the training direction across all five series (@tbl-external-program).

Program 5 had an adverse full-fit coefficient and enrichment for mitotic and
stromal-immune signatures. It was active in `r p7r$active_folds[p7r$program == 5]`
training folds. Its pooled external HR per training SD was
`r p5 <- subset(rd(K5, "prompt7_desurv_style", "program_hr.csv"), model == "w1" & program == 5); num(p5$hr[p5$cohort == "pooled"], 2)`
(donor-clustered 95% CI `r ci(p5$donor_lo[p5$cohort == "pooled"], p5$donor_hi[p5$cohort == "pooled"], 2)`),
opposite in direction to its training coefficient, and `r sum(p5$hr[p5$cohort != "pooled"] < 1)` of the
`r sum(p5$cohort != "pooled")` series had HRs below one. Its biological
interpretation is exploratory. Its activity in only
`r p7r$active_folds[p7r$program == 5]` training folds (@sec-program-stability) shows the same
instability.

## External program associations and risk groups {#sec-program-external}

Separate external Cox regressions give descriptive associations per series SD of each
active program score of the rank-5 fit. The numbers of estimates in the training direction, in program order,
were `r paste(vapply(split(program_external, program_external$program), function(x) sum(sign(x$log_hr) == x$training_sign), 0L), collapse = ", ")`
of `r nrow(e_w1)`. These estimates are marginal. The training coefficients condition on

```{r}
hr_table[paste("Program", names(hr_display))] <- hr_display
```

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

## Interpretation {#sec-interpretation}

The working model, the supervised YFB fit ($w_S = 1$, 2,218 genes, rank `r tcv_K`), had
cross-validated training concordance `r num(k5_cw$mean_YFB)` and a mean external concordance of
`r num(kp("equal_YFB")$estimate)`. Linking survival to the latent scores instead of the
projection changed neither number by more than 0.01. For the supervised YFB fit ($w_S = 1$,
2,218 genes, rank 5), the external concordance difference from the two-step fit was small and
its interval included zero. Its estimated loadings correlated 1.000 with the unsupervised
loadings at the unit survival weight. DeSurv and elastic-net Cox trained on the same patients
had the concordance differences and intervals shown in @tbl-comparators. The joint coefficient fit accounts for posterior loading uncertainty and
uses a shrinkage prior. Calibration slopes of the rank-5 fit and the two-step fit differed by
less than their standard errors in every series. The calibration slope is the coefficient of a Cox regression
of held-out survival on the fitted risk score, and a slope of one means the fitted risk
differences have the observed size.

In the rank-7 simulation cells with consistent recovery, the two-step fit already recovered the
prognostic program. The near-threshold simulations isolated a setting where supervision
could change discovery. Recovery and concordance improved when survival was strong, while
the differences were smaller at realistic survival strength. Methylation alone, on the matched
TCGA patients, had concordance close to 0.5, below expression in every comparison but mostly
within two standard errors. It added no survival-active program, although a few of its
programs are not explained by the expression programs.

## Limitations {#sec-limitations}

The gene screen, the input scaling, pooling without a cohort indicator and the starting-value
constraints were chosen with external concordance among the evidence before the
current selection procedure, and every external series informed at least one of the choices recorded in
the audit (@sec-external-uses). Training cross-validation now supports the screen and the
scaling and selected rank `r tcv_K` (@sec-results-rank). Because the external series informed
the screen and scaling first, the external results still describe a model whose setup those
cohorts helped choose. The rank and screen comparisons were repeated over five random
partitions of the same 273 patients. Four of the five partitions selected the same rank, so the choices depend little on how
patients are assigned to folds, but it does not measure sampling variability. The PACA-AU array and RNA-seq records both contribute to the pooled estimate. The donor bootstrap and the
donor-clustered HR intervals account for their shared donors while retaining both series in the
estimand. DeSurv used its published settings rather than a new search on our training folds.
All five supervised training folds converged at rank `r tcv_K`.

In the rank-7 simulations the coefficients at $w_S = 1$ are
attenuated at the larger gene count. These studies use a common simulation generator. The
simulation comparing the two survival links issued R warnings whose messages were not saved.
The methylation comparison has `r meth_aud$n` patients and screened and imputed its CpGs before
the folds were split. Its CpG–gene correlations are not adjusted for purity.

## Continuing work {#sec-continuing}

Proposed supervision weights include a power on the Cox partial likelihood chosen to match
the information in a correctly specified model, downweighting expression and normalizing the
likelihood terms. Each would be compared in simulation, on recovery of the planted program,
calibration slopes, convergence and the risk-score contribution of programs that match no
planted program, before application to the real data.

The working model uses rank `r tcv_K`, the projection link, point-Laplace priors on the scores and loadings and a Normal prior on each coefficient (@sec-week). The joint model for expression and methylation remains in development (@sec-week-multimodal). Its open problem is balancing the data types when CpG sites far outnumber genes, which a power on the reconstruction likelihood does not solve. Weighting methylation only in the score update and summarizing CpG sites by region are the next candidates, followed by joint fits at 10,000 and 100,000 sites judged mainly on the programs they find. Later choices will use simulation and training data as described in @sec-external-uses.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Appendix A. Model derivation {#sec-appendix-a .unnumbered}

The canonical single-modality procedure uses training expression $Y$ and survival times
and indicators. It returns posterior moments of $L$, $F$ and $\beta$, gene precisions
and the tracked variational objective.

1. Center and scale the input according to the training preprocessing recipe. Initialize the
   factorization using a truncated singular value decomposition of the resulting $Y$.
2. Compute the posterior mean and variance of $\eta$. Re-expand the Cox partial
   log-likelihood about the current mean predictor, using the diagonal curvature to
   obtain a working normal-means objective.
3. For each program, update $\beta_k$ using the first and second moments of $YF_k$.
   Update $L_k$ from the expression residual. Update the entries of $F_k$ using both
   likelihood contributions and refresh the projected scores within the loading update.
   Use empirical Bayes normal-means fits for the prior parameters.
4. Update the gene-specific noise precisions. Record the monitored objective including
   the weighted Cox term and the Kullback–Leibler terms. Rescale nonzero programs
   to unit training projection SD and check the relative change in the objective.
5. In each external series, apply the fixed projection loadings and coefficients to
   the available training genes. Harrell's concordance uses the direction learned
   from training survival.

The [full derivation](../../../derivations/SSBMF-YFB-model-derivations/SSBMF-YFB-model-derivation-full.pdf)
gives the update formulas, the balance of expression and survival information and the
numerical checks. The companion `verify_derivation.R` evaluates individual updates against
the expected objective.

This version reports the rank-5 working model and its rebuilt external comparisons, risk groups and program exhibits. It adds the prior comparisons, methylation analysis, survival-link comparison, training-only screen and rank analysis, weight refit and descriptive multimodal comparison. The prior and input-scaling comparisons use the rank-7 reference. The simulation exhibits keep their designs, which fit rank 7.

# Appendix D. Sensitivity to the priors {#sec-appendix-d .unnumbered}

Both comparisons use the rank-7 reference (@sec-model-states) and compare priors with each
other, not each prior against an absolute standard. Their full results are in
`docs/findings/2026-11-12-lf-prior-comparison-findings.md`,
`docs/findings/2026-11-12-lf-prior-followup-findings.md` and
`docs/findings/2026-11-12-beta-prior-comparison-findings.md`.

## Priors on the scores and loadings {.unnumbered}

The current model uses point-Laplace priors on $L$ and $F$ with expression z-scored within each
cohort. The alternative is a point-exponential prior, which keeps every score and loading
nonnegative, as in a nonnegative matrix factorization. It needs nonnegative input, so expression
is divided by each gene's within-cohort standard deviation without centering, and the Cox
projection is centered on the training data. Everything else is the rank-7 reference's: $w_S = 1$,
a Normal coefficient prior, $K = 7$ without pruning, at most 300 sweeps and tolerance $10^{-5}$.
The simulation uses the three variance cells of the fixed-weight simulation at 2,000 genes and
the strong-survival cell of the near-threshold simulation at a planted share of 0.05%, with
`r prior_n_sim` datasets each. The planted scores and loadings are exponential, so the truth
favors neither prior. The training comparison uses the five folds of @sec-results-fair on the
pooled `r prior_n_train` patients and counts only pairs of patients from the same cohort.

In simulation the point-exponential prior recovered the planted program as often as
point-Laplace, and more often near the detection threshold (`r lf_pe$recovered[1]` against
`r lf_pl$recovered[1]` of `r prior_n_sim`), and every fit converged (@tbl-lf-prior-sim). The
point-exponential prior also marked more programs survival-active that matched no planted
program, with means of `r num(min(lf_pe$mean_false_active), 1)` to
`r num(max(lf_pe$mean_false_active), 1)` per fit against `r num(min(lf_pl$mean_false_active), 1)`
to `r num(max(lf_pl$mean_false_active), 1)` for point-Laplace. Such programs are expected, and in
the shifted-input fits, where their size was measured, their coefficients were mostly a tenth to
a quarter of the planted program's.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lf-prior-sim
#| tbl-cap: "Point-Laplace and point-exponential priors on the scores and loadings in simulation at 2,000 genes. Entries give point-Laplace first and point-exponential second. Recovered and converged are counts of datasets. False-active is the mean number of false-active programs per fit. Validation C and the calibration slope are medians over datasets. The 0.05% cell is the strong-survival cell of the near-threshold simulation."
pair_cell <- function(a, b, d) paste(num(a, d), num(b, d), sep = " / ")
kable(data.frame(`Planted share` = unname(cell_share),
  Recovered = paste(lf_pl$recovered, lf_pe$recovered, sep = " / "),
  `False-active programs` = pair_cell(lf_pl$mean_false_active, lf_pe$mean_false_active, 1),
  Converged = paste(lf_pl$converged, lf_pe$converged, sep = " / "),
  `Validation C` = pair_cell(lf_pl$median_c_validation, lf_pe$median_c_validation, 3),
  `Calibration slope` = pair_cell(lf_pl$median_cal_slope, lf_pe$median_cal_slope, 2),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lccccc")
```

On the training data the point-exponential fit lost concordance and described the difference
between the cohorts (@tbl-lf-prior-real). Dividing by the within-cohort standard deviation keeps
each cohort's mean level. The median gene mean was `r num(gene_mean_xsd[["TCGA_PAAD"]], 1)` in
TCGA-PAAD and `r num(gene_mean_xsd[["CPTAC"]], 1)` in CPTAC, against a within-cohort standard
deviation of 1. In every fold one program's scores correlated at least
`r num(min(lf_fits$max_abs_cor_cohort[lf_fits$arm == "PE" & lf_fits$fold > 0]))` with cohort
membership, and no program was survival-active. Three further setups removed or absorbed that
difference. Cohort strata center the projection and the baseline hazard within each cohort. A
shifted z-score adds to each gene's z-scores a constant equal to minus their minimum over the
`r prior_n_train` patients, so the input is nonnegative and both cohorts have the same gene means. The shift constants use
all training patients, held-out folds included, and they enter the reconstruction, so a refitted
model can change with them.
The within-patient rank transform used by DeSurv ranks the genes within each patient and divides
each gene's ranks by their within-cohort standard deviation. Each setup recovered part of the
lost concordance, but all stayed below point-Laplace by more than one standard error, and no
setup converged in more than `r max(lf_real[pe_alt, "conv"])` of 5 folds within 300 sweeps. The
shifted z-score removed the association with cohort, but in simulation it behaved like the
unshifted point-exponential fit, with `r num(min(lf_sz$mean_false_active), 1)` to
`r num(max(lf_sz$mean_false_active), 1)` false-active programs per fit. Under strata the programs
still correlate `r num(lf_real["PES", "cohort_cor"])` with cohort membership, so they still
separate the two cohorts, and the strata absorb that offset only in the survival model. The
programs keep the loading directions of the unstratified fit, with larger column norms. The
point-Laplace prior is kept, because it predicted better on the training data. At rank `r tcv_K`, the rank selected in @sec-results-rank, the
point-exponential prior on expression divided by its within-cohort standard deviation gave
within-cohort concordance `r num(tcv_a$mean_C_within_PE)` against
`r num(tcv_a$mean_C_within_PL)` for point-Laplace.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lf-prior-real
#| tbl-cap: "Priors on the scores and loadings in five-fold training cross-validation. Concordance counts only pairs of patients from the same cohort. The difference from the current model is paired over folds, with its standard error. Convergence is within 300 sweeps. Survival-active programs are the range over folds. Cohort correlation is the largest absolute correlation of a program's training scores with cohort membership over folds. Under strata the cohort offset is absorbed by the stratified baseline hazard."
lf_lab <- c(PL = "Point-Laplace, z-scores within cohort, rank 7",
            PE = "Point-exponential, divided by within-cohort SD",
            PES = "Point-exponential, divided by within-cohort SD, cohort strata",
            SZ = "Point-exponential, shifted z-scores",
            RANK = "Point-exponential, within-patient ranks")
lf_tab <- lf_real[names(lf_lab), ]
kable(data.frame(`Prior and input` = unname(lf_lab), `Mean C` = num(lf_tab$C),
  `Difference (SE)` = c("", paste0(num(lf_diff[names(lf_lab)[-1], "diff_within"]), " (",
                                   num(lf_diff[names(lf_lab)[-1], "se_within"]), ")")),
  `Folds converged` = paste0(lf_tab$conv, "/5"),
  `Survival-active programs` = ifelse(lf_tab$act_lo == lf_tab$act_hi, lf_tab$act_lo,
                                      paste(lf_tab$act_lo, "to", lf_tab$act_hi)),
  `Cohort correlation` = sapply(lf_tab$cohort_cor, function(x) num(x, if (x < 0.5) 2 else 3)),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lccccc")
```

## Prior on the survival coefficients {.unnumbered}

The current model gives each coefficient its own Normal prior. The alternatives are a
point-Laplace and a point-normal prior, either of which can set a coefficient exactly to zero. A
prior with a point mass cannot be estimated from one coefficient, so both are shared across the
seven programs. A shared Normal prior separates the effect of sharing from that of sparsity. All
other settings, the simulation cells and the folds are those of the comparison above, with
point-Laplace priors on the scores and loadings.

The four priors gave nearly the same fits (@tbl-beta-prior). The sparse priors lowered false
activity slightly where the planted program was clear, to
`r num(b_cells$B_PN$mean_false_active[2], 1)` against `r num(b_cells$PL$mean_false_active[2], 1)`
at a share of `r cell_share[[2]]`. Median calibration slopes differed by at most
`r num(max(b_slope_spread[prior_cells != "s9_5pct"]), 2)` between priors outside the 5% cell. In
training cross-validation the shared point-Laplace prior lowered concordance by
`r num(-b_pair$diff_within[b_pair$arm == "B_PLAP"])` (SE
`r num(b_pair$se_within[b_pair$arm == "B_PLAP"])`), and the shared point-normal prior by
`r num(-b_pair$diff_within[b_pair$arm == "B_PN"])` (SE
`r num(b_pair$se_within[b_pair$arm == "B_PN"])`). Under the shared point-normal prior, the
posterior probability that a coefficient is nonzero was between `r num(min(b_pip_full$pip), 2)`
and `r num(max(b_pip_full$pip), 2)` for all seven programs in the full training fit, so it did
not single out the `r length(b_active_full)` survival-active programs. In simulation the mean
number of programs per fit with an inclusion probability above 0.5 was
`r num(b_pn_incl[["s9_0.25pct"]], 1)` at a share of 0.25% and
`r num(b_pn_incl[["s9_1pct"]], 1)` at the larger shares, so the prior picked out the planted
program alone when that program was clear. Near the threshold it was
`r num(b_pn_incl[["s14_0.05pct"]], 1)`. The Normal prior is kept.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-beta-prior
#| tbl-cap: "Coefficient priors in simulation at 2,000 genes and in five-fold training cross-validation. Point-Laplace priors on the scores and loadings throughout. Simulation entries give the planted programs recovered and the mean number of false-active programs per fit. Every simulated fit converged. Training concordance counts pairs within cohort, and the difference from the Normal prior is paired over folds."
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(b_cells$B_PN$mean_false_active[2], b_cells$B_PLAP$mean_false_active[2])),
          isTRUE(all.equal(b_pn_incl[["s9_1pct"]], b_pn_incl[["s9_5pct"]])))
sim_rows <- t(sapply(names(b_arms), function(a)
  paste0(b_cells[[a]]$recovered, ", ", num(b_cells[[a]]$mean_false_active, 1))))
b_d <- c(PL = "", setNames(paste0(num(b_pair$diff_within), " (", num(b_pair$se_within), ")"),
                           b_pair$arm))[names(b_arms)]
b_tab <- rbind(t(sim_rows), num(b_C), b_d, num(b_active, 1), paste0(b_conv, "/5"))
b_tab <- data.frame(Measure = c(paste0("Simulation, ", cell_share, " share: recovered, false-active"),
                                "Training CV: mean C", "Difference from Normal (SE)",
                                "Survival-active programs per fold", "Folds converged"),
                    b_tab, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
names(b_tab)[-1] <- unname(b_arms)
names(b_tab)[2] <- "Normal, rank 7"
kable(b_tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "lcccc")
```
